changes: NOTHING WAS CHANGED. This is not a transcription: the manufacturer serves this model as a text file, so it was frozen byte-for-byte under vendor/ and the whole file - model text and the vendor's own comment blocks - was appended below a header of our own. No parameter was removed (unlike models/jfet/lsk489.lib and models/bjt_pnp/ls350.lib, where mfg= had to be stripped because ngspice evaluates it as an expression and dies; this file has no mfg=), no value was rounded, reordered or 'corrected', and the model NAME was left exactly as served. Verifiable rather than asserted: diff <(grep -v '^\*' <vendor file>) <(grep -v '^\*' <this file>) is empty. One consequence worth knowing: the vendor file uses CRLF and our header uses LF, so the assembled file has MIXED line endings. That is deliberate - normalising the whole file rewrites the vendor bytes and breaks the diff above, silently. It happened once during L25 and only the diff caught it.
reason: T7 (ADR-016), NC-017. This device is instantiated FIVE times per gain block - tail current sink, the two ADR-014 cascodes, the VAS load and the Vbe multiplier (circuits/preamp/gain_block.py:262, 291, 292, 328, 350) - which makes it the most-used active part in the design. ADR-017 keeps the 2N5551 die and changes manufacturer and package: MMBT5551, Diodes Incorporated, SOT-23.
notes: CROSS-CHECK AGAINST THE VENDOR'S OWN DATASHEET (DS30061 Rev. 15-2, 2025), ngspice 47, set temp = 25: hFE 107.218 at IC = 10 mA, VCE = 5 V (window 80..250, INSIDE); fT 175.683 MHz at IC = 10 mA, VCE = 10 V, ftest = 100 MHz (100 MHz min, INSIDE); C_obo 2.2207 pF at VCB = 10 V, 1 MHz (6 pF max, INSIDE). THREE OF THREE INSIDE. ON THIS DEVICE THE fT DEFINITION MATTERS, where on the MMBT5401 it did not: the datasheet defines fT as the gain-bandwidth product measured at ftest = 100 MHz, which gives 175.683 MHz, while the |hfe| = 1 crossing gives 172.579 MHz, 1.8% lower. The roll-off is not a clean -20 dB/dec to unity - GBW peaks at 176.9 MHz near 30 MHz and falls to 105 MHz by 1 GHz. The datasheet's definition is the one locked, because it is what the 100 MHz minimum refers to. L24 recorded 173.1 MHz. Bias verified: op prints IC = 1.000000e-02. QUASIMOD, RCO, VO and GAMMA are accepted by ngspice with zero warnings (verified by running it). The vendor writes 'RB =0.26' and 'RE =0.23' with a space before the equals sign and that space is KEPT; ngspice parses it. NO KF/AF, therefore NO 1/f noise - in this repo only models/jfet/lsk489.lib has flicker noise, which is why NC-004 does not close when the real models arrive. Any noise figure computed with this device is a floor without flicker and must say so next to the number.
